observations:
Torah LM2:43 is one of the shortest in Likutay Moharan Tinyana — three sentences that form a tight, self-contained teaching. A thorough scan for bechina-connected concept clusters beyond the two identified packages yields no candidates for a third independent domain.

The Torah's entire argument operates within two thematic poles:

1. Package 1 (גְּבוּרָה וְחֹזֶק הַלֵּב): The domain of inner heroism — the essential unity of bravery (גְּבוּרָה), strong-heartedness (חֹזֶק לֵב), courage (אֹמֶץ לֵב), and the warrior archetype (גִּבּוֹר). These are explicitly equated through bechina language.

2. Package 2 (חֲלִישׁוּת הַלֵּב וְהַיִּרְאָה): The evil mirror — the essential unity of weakness of heart (חֲלִישׁוּת הַלֵּב), soft-heartedness (רַךְ לֵבָב), the fearful person (הַיָּרֵא), and fear/terror (פַּחַד).

Candidates reviewed and rejected:

- 'Battle / war' (קִשְׁרֵי הַמִּלְחָמָה): The Rebbe mentions 'runs into the bonds of battle' as an action of the גִּבּוֹר. However, this is an eitza consequence of Package 1 (the strong-hearted warrior runs into battle because of his strength), not a bechina cluster with its own domain. There is no bechina language equating מִלְחָמָה with other concepts, and it appears only once as an example, not as a structural pole.

- 'The verse / Torah proof' (אִישׁ הַיָּרֵא וְרַךְ הַלֵּבָב, Devarim 20:8): The Rebbe cites this verse and Rashi's gloss as external prooftexts for Package 2's bechina equations. The verse itself is not a new conceptual domain — it is evidence for the existing package structure.

- 'Lev (heart) as neutral structural node': One might propose a neutral 'heart' package as a structural metaphor that can be filled with either strength or weakness. However, in this Torah the לֵב is never used neutrally — it always appears in one of its two polarized states (חָזָק or רַךְ/חָלָשׁ). There is no bechina language equating לֵב with a third domain independent of the two polarities. The heart here is the field of battle between the two packages, not an independent package.

Conclusion: The two packages (good: bravery/strong-heart; evil: weakness/fear) fully exhaust the bechina topology of this Torah. The teaching is structurally binary — a paired good/evil mirror with a single 'וְכֵן לְהֵפֶךְ' (and conversely) transition between them. No third independent domain exists with 3+ bechina-connected nodes.
